exclusion_detail: The 6-methoxyindole-2-carboxylic acid is prepared in the paper (cited to ref 51, no procedure), not bought (second reader). (Reclassified 2026-10-24 after the verification pass.)

lead.label: C7
lead.why: Among them, compound C7 (IC50 = 0.16 uM) exhibited the most potent anti-proliferative activity against HCT116 cells ... compound C7 could be a potential lead compound

reactions.conditions: General procedure 4.1: oridonin (0.1 mmol), carboxylic acid (0.15 mmol), EDCI (0.3 mmol), DMAP (10 mg), dry CH2Cl2, 25 C, 2-8 h; chromatography; yield 87% for C7
reactions.source: Main article Sections 2.1 and 4.1 (general procedure) and 4.1.19 (C7 characterisation); Scheme 2

notes: FLAT SMILES: the printed names carry full stereochemistry (oridonin is a chiral ent-kaurane); I did not write stereo in SMILES because I could not verify it, so compare with stereo ignored. Oridonin SMILES was derived by hand from the ent-kaurane skeleton (C20H28O6, 14-OH on the one-carbon bridge) and checked by atom count only. Oridonin name 'oridonin' is the paper's own term. CAVEAT for reviewer: Scheme 1 says the indole-2-carboxylic acids 8a-8i were prepared (benzaldehyde + ethyl 2-azidoacetate, cyclisation, NaOH hydrolysis, ref 51) but NO procedure for them is given in the main text or SI (SI is NMR spectra only); the Experimental says all chemicals were purchased. 6-Methoxyindole-2-carboxylic acid is a stock chemical so I treated it as a commercial leaf; under a strict reading of the brief (prepared as reported, no procedure) this paper could instead be route_not_explicit. Reactants of C7 are the two listed; EDCI/DMAP are coupling reagents leaving no atoms.
